Implement the following feature request in this repository (oneDAL).

# cosine_distance: support self-distances with a single input table

scikit-learn-intelex wants to compute `cosine_distances(X)` (all pairwise distances between the rows of one table) through oneDAL without passing the data twice. Today `oneapi::dal::compute(desc, x, y)` requires both tables, and an empty `y` is rejected.

Requested:
- `cosine_distance::compute_input` gets a constructor that takes only `x`, so `dal::compute(desc, x)` works (with the host and the device policy overloads the other algorithms have).
- `compute(desc, x)` and `compute(desc, x, table{})` return the same n x n matrix as `compute(desc, x, x)`.
- On CPU, the single-table case should use the DAAL cosine-distance kernel that takes one input table (it already exists and is the fast path daal4py uses) instead of treating it as a two-table call.
- Existing two-table behaviour and its argument checks are unchanged, except that an empty `y` is no longer an error. `bazel` is on PATH; this machine has no GPU. Do not weaken or delete existing tests.
